free_text: The patient is a 66-year-old male with a high PSA of 8.3 and a cT3b prostate cancer, confirmed by a Gleason 3+5 pathology. MRI showed a PI-RADS 5 lesion with extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle involvement. Given the high-risk local staging and biochemical status, individual treatment benefit and patient preferences require clinical review. The trade-off involves balancing aggressive local control against potential side effects of definitive treatment.
